candidates.question: For each i, if there are multiple K-element subsets containing A_i that achieve the same maximum GCD, is any specific formatting required for the output?
candidates.answer: No, just output the single maximum GCD value for each i.

candidates.question: Is the output order strictly for i from 1 to N, or can it be in any order as long as each i is accounted for?
candidates.answer: The output must be in order from i=1 to i=N, each on its own line.

candidates.question: If K = 1, is the answer for each i simply A_i itself?
candidates.answer: Yes, because the only K-element subset containing A_i is {A_i}, and its GCD is A_i.

candidates.question: If multiple elements in A have the same value, can they be chosen as distinct elements in the K-element subset?
candidates.answer: Yes, each occurrence is a distinct element, so you can choose multiple copies if they exist.

candidates.question: Are there any constraints on the running time or memory usage beyond the given limits?
candidates.answer: No explicit constraints beyond typical competitive programming expectations given N up to 1.2e6.

candidates.question: Can the input contain zeros or negative numbers?
candidates.answer: No, A_i are positive integers between 1 and 10^6.

candidates.question: If N = K, is the answer for each i simply the GCD of the entire array?
candidates.answer: Yes, because the only K-element subset containing A_i is the whole array.

candidates.question: Should the GCD be computed as a positive integer even if some chosen elements are zero?
candidates.answer: All A_i are positive, so the GCD will always be a positive integer.
